To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dry-thermophlic anaerobic digestion was stable and efficient when the total solid (TS)-content in the reactor was between ca. 18-28%, but the TS-content in the reactor should be controlled below 30% to prevent accumulation of propionate.
the dry thermophilic AD process is stable and can achieve a high biogas production rate at a substrate TS level of 32% (representing 36% of water addition) and reactor TS of 23%.

the TS content of dry thermophilic digesters can be increased from the current maximum of 30-32% without affecting biogas production, and that this can be achieved by reducing the amount of water in the substrate from 36% to 18%.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a novel dry anaerobic diges-ter that can achieve stable biogas produc-tion at a substrate TS of 32% and a reactor TS of 23%, which is much higher than the TS content in most of the conventional anaerobic digesters (10-25% TS).
the effect of substrate TS content on the stability and performance of dry thermophilic biogas production.
the influence of TS content on dry anaerobic digestion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the TS content of substrate should not exceed 32%, and that of the reactor should not exceed 23% in order to maintain a stable and high biogas production in a dry thermophilic semi-batch anaerobic digeser.
the TS content in dry anaerobic digestion can be reduced to 30% of the total solid substrate.
dry thermophilic AD can achieve stable and efficient methane production at TS content of 18-27% in the reactor, which can reduce the water addition to 0.3-0.5 times of the total substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a TS content of the substrate of 32% (TS content of the reactor 23%) is the upper limit for stable and high biogas production in dry-thermophic anaerobic digesters fed with rice straw and pig waste.
the dry thermophilic AD of rice straw and manure can be stable and effective at a substrate TS of 32% and a reactor TS of 23%.
the TS content of dry anaerobic digested substrate could be increased to 42% without affecting biogas production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high TS content of the substrate (32%) can be used in dry anaerobic digestion without the risk of reactor instability.

the TS content of a dry anaerobic digested reactor can be increased up to 23% by adding a small amount of water (10% of the total amount of substrate), which will reduce the amount of water needed for the process.
the amount of water that is added to a dry thermophilic digester can be reduced to 36% of the substrate weight, and the digester can operate stably at a reactor TS content of 23%.
